column3: unicon 13.3 takes the program (a class whose lines carry no semicolons) and prints m, rc 0, since it inserts a semicolon at a newline; SCRIP refuses it, rc 1, error 703 end missing semicolon or operator at line 4. This is Lon's law of 2026-11-10 (skill unicon section 4: every vendored Unicon file carries its semicolons, committed once, no program adds them), so the ref is unicon's own answer and the refusal is the law, graded every lap on the plain form by the twelve icont refusals of gate_cases_icon (cto's ruling 2026-11-18, MEASURED on SCRIP 559cf5e95)

unicon 13.3 takes the program (a statement ended by a newline in a body, under the dialect switch) and prints 1, rc 0, since it inserts a semicolon at a newline; SCRIP refuses it under --dialect=unicon, rc 1, error 703 write missing semicolon or operator at line 3. This is Lon's law of 2026-11-10 (skill unicon section 4: every vendored Unicon file carries its semicolons, committed once, no program adds them), so the ref is unicon's own answer and the refusal is the law, graded every lap on the plain form by the twelve icont refusals of gate_cases_icon (cto's ruling 2026-11-18, MEASURED on SCRIP 559cf5e95)
